title: Eleven Biscuits and One Tin
subtitle: 饼干与甜食 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饼干与甜食（生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饼干与甜食（生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：cookie　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cookie 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my grandmother ① baked a cookie that nobody in the house had asked for, and she said the baking was the whole of the afternoon. The ② cookie, meaning the biscuit and not the tin, was eleven to a tray and stayed that number; cookie, she said, is the only thing in a kitchen that is judged by how few are left at night.

Every ③ cookie in that tin had the same shape, and the ④ cookie at the end, meaning the one she kept for the visitors and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever declined twice. Cookie, my mother said, is nine parts shape and one part somebody willing to offer; my grandmother said the offering is the part that fills the tin.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the cookie was the whole of the machine, meaning the little file and not the biscuit. The ⑥ cookie, meaning the little file and not any of that, is the only thing on a machine that everybody accepts and nobody reads; cookie, he said, is either something you bake or the only word that means both a biscuit and a little file. She said the little file is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ cookie had become a line in a recipe book, and the book had become an argument about the shape. The ⑧ cookie of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in October, was one tray and thirty years of offering; cookie, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to offer. He said the offering was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cookie I remember is the one at the end, which she baked in 1972 and is still described as the roundest in the county. A ⑩ cookie, my mother said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being shared; every cookie, she said, is a little file that has agreed to look like a biscuit. She said the little file was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 曲奇饼；小甜饼
B. n. 饼干（指那一块饼干本身，与那只罐子相对）
C. 固定搭配：bake a cookie 烤一块饼干
D. n. 饼干（指那只罐子里每一块）
E. n. 饼干（指末尾那一块）
F. n. 小型数据文件；Cookie（计算机用语）
G. n. 饼干（指食谱里提到的那一块）
H. n. 点心；饼干（抽象总称）

items.q: baked a cookie that nobody in the house had asked for
The cookie, meaning the biscuit and not the tin
the cookie was the whole of the machine
The cookie, meaning the little file
the cookie had become a line in a recipe book
The cookie of the whole thing
A cookie, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: bake a cookie 意为“烤一块饼干”，1958 年祖母烤了一块家里谁也没要过的饼干。
cookie 意为“饼干”，指那一块饼干本身而不是那只罐子，一盘十一个。
cookie 指那只罐子里每一块饼干，每一块都是同样的形状。
cookie 指末尾那一块（她留给客人的那一块），是唯一有人推辞过两次的。
cookie 意为“小型数据文件、Cookie”，父亲说 Cookie 就是那台机器的全部，指的是网站存的小文件而不是那块饼干。
cookie 为计算机用语，指浏览器里存的小文件而不是那块饼干，是机器上人人都接受、却无人阅读的东西。
cookie 意为“饼干”，指食谱里提到的那一块，到 1966 年这块饼干成了食谱里的一行。
cookie 意为“点心、饼干”，祖母十月写道，整件事的点心是一盘饼干三十年的拿出来待客。
cookie 意为“曲奇饼、小甜饼”，我记得的是末尾那一块，她 1972 年烤的，至今仍被说成全县最圆的。
cookie 为抽象总称，母亲说一块饼干是唯一会因为被分享而变好的东西。
